name: Ali Bahadur II
role: Nawab of Banda and rebel ally in Bundelkhand
contribution: Ali Bahadur II, the Nawab of Banda, joined the anti-Company coalition in Bundelkhand during the Indian Rebellion of 1857 and supported rebel resistance in north-central India.
context: His position connected the rebellion's military politics with the claims of regional courts and displaced ruling houses. Bundelkhand's conflict formed part of the wider 1857–1859 uprising but followed its own alliances and military campaigns.
impact: Ali Bahadur II is remembered as one of the regional rulers who challenged East India Company authority in 1857. His story highlights the coalition-building and local political claims that shaped the rebellion beyond its major urban centres.
highlight: Nawab of Banda who joined the Bundelkhand resistance against East India Company rule in 1857.
seoTitle: Ali Bahadur II: Nawab of Banda in the 1857 Rebellion
seoDescription: Learn about Ali Bahadur II, the Nawab of Banda who joined the Bundelkhand resistance during the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
shortAnswer: Ali Bahadur II was the Nawab of Banda and a regional ally of the anti-Company rebellion in Bundelkhand during 1857.

faq.question: Who was Ali Bahadur II?
faq.answer: He was the Nawab of Banda who joined rebel resistance against East India Company rule in Bundelkhand during the 1857 uprising.

faq.question: Why is Ali Bahadur II relevant to 1857 history?
faq.answer: His role shows how regional rulers and political allies joined the wider rebellion while pursuing local claims and alliances in Bundelkhand.
